citation.title: Efficacy and safety of ketone ester infusion to prevent muscle weakness in a mouse model of sepsis-induced critical illness

interpretation: Retain dose- and preparation-specific nominal benefits in ex vivo CSA-normalized EDL force in day-5 survivors, alongside severe dose/route-dependent toxicity and largely persistent atrophy. The only continuous-infusion preparation is the 50:50 R,R/S,S mixture. This is not evidence for D-only infusion, human clinical benefit, whole-animal functional rescue, or BUB1B/MVA rescue.

formulations.exact_identity: 50:50 mixture of the two pure R,R and S,S 3HHB esters
formulations.boundary: Not sodium D,L-3HB salt; not unspecified four-stereoisomer material; continuous infusion cannot be credited to R,R alone.

model_and_design.model: 5-day centrally catheterized, fluid-resuscitated cecal ligation/puncture sepsis
model_and_design.randomization: Supplement reports random allocation to healthy/sepsis and within sepsis to placebo/ester in experiments 1 and 3; sequence-generation/concealment detail not reported. Experiment 2 is separately described; within-dose randomization not established.
model_and_design.blinding: Caretakers and data collectors blinded to group allocation.
model_and_design.support: Balanced fluid/hydroxyethyl starch during first 20 hours; antibiotics and buprenorphine every 12 hours; mixed parenteral nutrition Olimel N7E 5.8 kcal/day from day 1.
model_and_design.hierarchy: Muscle force is the stated efficacy focus and sample-size basis; no prospective registered endpoint hierarchy or SAP verified.
model_and_design.sampling: Sequential dose escalation; each dose step included healthy and placebo controls, presented pooled. In absence of toxicity, continued until 14 day-5 survivors with force measurements.
model_and_design.exclusions: A priori physical abnormality before surgery, surgery death, pre-randomization death, or catheter malfunction; per-reason excluded counts not given. Included survival denominators are not independently verified as all initially allocated animals.
model_and_design.selection: Force, tissue and endpoint blood outcomes are conditional on day-5 survival. Numbers sometimes differ from surviving counts; missing-assay reasons are not supplied.
model_and_design.analysis: ANOVA with Fisher LSD/Student t post hoc, transformations as needed; Wilcoxon for nonnormal data, chi-square mortality, MANOVA for kinetic profiles. Explicitly no multiple-comparison correction.

controls_and_exposure.bolus: Twice-daily subcutaneous administration from day 1. D/L source daily-dose labels 10, 20, 40, 80 mmol/kg/day; mixture 20, 40, 80. Isovolumetric glucose/Plasmalyte placebo, main 187.5 mg/day; supplement 6.25 mg/g/day. Not established isocaloric across ester doses.
controls_and_exposure.infusion: Mixture only, 40 or 80 mmol/kg/day from day 1; PN 0.2 mL/h plus ester/vehicle 0.033 mL/h via a catheter with non-return valves.
controls_and_exposure.unresolved_control_unit_discrepancy: Supplement page 3 prints infusion D-glucose 6.25 mg/kg/day; page 2 prints bolus 6.25 mg/g/day and main gives bolus 187.5 mg/day. The 1000-fold difference in weight-normalized units remains unresolved; no correction or caloric equivalence assumed.
controls_and_exposure.kinetics: Separate experiment with healthy/day-2 septic mice after D-ester bolus at source daily-dose labels 40 or 80 mmol/kg/day; samples at 30, 45, 60, 180 minutes. Single-injection amount should not be inferred by silently converting the daily-dose labels.

experiment1.counts_sources: Main Figures 1–4 captions; native Figure 1 and Supplement Figure S1. Zero terminal endpoint counts at 80 reflect all deaths, not measured nulls.

specific_force.effect: higher than placebo; reported 93% of healthy control level
higher than placebo; reported 93% of healthy control level
higher than placebo; reported 90% of healthy control level

experiment1.force_nulls: D10, L10, D20 and DL20 were not significantly improved versus placebo; L40 has no placebo-difference marker in native Figure 2a and no reported significant force benefit. No force assessment survives in any 80 bolus arm.
experiment1.other_positives: D10 has lower illness score with a P≤.05 versus-placebo marker in native Figure 1b (exact P not supplied). DL40 attenuated tibialis loss and L40 attenuated EDL loss, each P=.01 versus placebo; L40 also increased illness/mortality. D20/L20 had lower creatinine than placebo (P≤.03).
experiment1.harms: All 80 bolus arms died (D 8/8, L 8/8, DL 7/7; P<.0001 versus placebo). L40 illness P=.01 and mortality P=.05 versus placebo (10/24 versus 23/103). D20/DL20 raised sodium (P≤.02); L40 lowered bicarbonate (P≤.0001). Native Figure 4c shows greater histological liver-damage distributions at D10 and L10 (text P≤.02).
experiment1.nulls: Most muscle-mass loss persisted; Trim63/Fbxo32 upregulation was unchanged versus placebo (P≥.1). TNFα did not improve (P≥.07); liver triglycerides were similar (P≥.1). GGT similar (P≥.4), reported as data not shown. These nulls do not establish absence of harm.
experiment1.reporting_caution: The discussion’s broad claims of no electrolyte or histological harm are qualified by the explicit Results/native Figure 3/4 findings above.

experiment2.count_gap: Main/native Figure 5 supplies total N=27 only; Methods says at least five per concentration, but exact healthy/septic by-dose analyzed counts are not reported.
experiment2.outcomes: D-3HB exposure/time profiles indicated slower apparent clearance in sepsis at both source dose labels: 40 P=.04; 80 P=.02. At 80 neither healthy nor septic mice cleared the rise by 180 minutes.
experiment2.limits: Only D-3HB measured. No L-3HB, circulating intact ester, 1,3-butanediol, or urinary mass balance; no formal clearance parameters/CI. Do not attribute observed lethality to a proven specific metabolite mechanism.

experiment3.counts_sources: Native Figure 6b gives placebo 15/17, DL40 17/21, DL80 14/19 survivors/total; healthy n15 in captions. Figure 6c/d and S3/S4 terminal n15/15/17/14.

specific_force.effect: numerically higher but not conventionally significant; reported trend

experiment3.mortality_and_illness: No significant difference versus placebo (mortality P≥.2; illness P≥.7). Deaths are still 2/17 placebo, 4/21 DL40, 5/19 DL80; this is not equivalence or zero mortality.
experiment3.other_outcomes: Plasma D-3HB increased dose dependently (P≤.0001); no muscle-mass benefit. Sodium/bicarbonate/glucose/creatinine had no detected difference versus placebo (P≥.2).
experiment3.route_comparison_limit: Bolus and infusion were separate experiments with different cohorts/control pools; no randomized direct route contrast or route-by-dose interaction established. Infusion evidence applies only to the mixture.

force_measurement.endpoint: Ex vivo EDL maximal isometric tetanic specific force on day 5
force_measurement.normalization: Absolute force divided by estimated cross-sectional area; CSA=muscle mass/[1.06 mg/mm³ × optimal fibre length], fibre length=0.44×resting optimal length.
force_measurement.caption_inconsistency: Captions say per unit muscle mass; main/supplement Methods and native axes explicitly support CSA normalization.
force_measurement.absolute_force: Figure 2b is a representative absolute-force trace (DL40), not a group-level absolute treatment contrast.
force_measurement.effect_precision: Group plots show means±SEM; no numerically reported between-group force difference or CI. Healthy-percent descriptions are not treatment differences. No plot digitization or equivalence interpretation.
force_measurement.transfer: No locomotion/endurance/whole-animal strength assay, no human sepsis trial, no BUB1B/BUBR1 expression/function or MVA model in this source.

lineage.packet: External primary packet lineage/lineage.json; see source bindings below.
lineage.confirmed_reuse: PMC8285799 (2021 cholesterol) explicitly reuses absolute-force measurements from PMC6600878 (2019). These are D,L-3HB sodium-salt data, not ester data.
lineage.endpoint_crosswalk: Overall healthy/placebo/salt survivor counts 15/17/17 match; 2019 specific-force n15/16/14 differs from 2021 overall captions. Exact animal-by-assay identity remains unavailable.
lineage.other_experiments: PMC8454128 (2021 salt toxicity) and the 2022 ester series describe their own experiments without located reuse statements; complete animal/control independence is not proven. Do not count four papers as four independent force replications.
lineage.scope: Bounded lineage appraisal, not full efficacy reappraisal of all earlier papers.

depth: Complete scientific main via official full XML; native Figures 1–6 viewed; all 10 supplement pages viewed including methods, design diagram, Table S1 and Figures S1–S4. Earlier papers only at the delegated lineage depth.
remaining_gaps: Missing-assay/exclusion counts and individual animal mapping

competitiveness.credit: Actual disease-model muscle-force evidence adds a direct muscle endpoint beyond sports performance. Preserve nominal preparation-specific positives; survivor conditioning does not prove the gains are artifacts.
competitiveness.limits: CSA-normalized force among survivors is not whole-cohort survival/function benefit, absolute force restoration or durable renewal. Uncorrected tests, pooled controls, assay missingness and severe exposure-dependent harms constrain advancement.
competitiveness.RR: Refines the existing exact R,R monoester appraisal. The R,R bolus result does not inherit mixture-only infusion effects or an oral sepsis effect.
competitiveness.SS: Separate exploratory preclinical preparation. A nominal gain at a lower tested dose than R,R does not establish superior clinical potency; the next reported dose increased illness/mortality.
competitiveness.mixture: Separate 50:50 R,R/S,S preparation. Nominal infusion force benefit at one exposure has no demonstrated mortality equivalence or direct randomized route comparison.
competitiveness.leaders: Niacin/restoration and apitegromab/compensation remain provisional. No head-to-head or MVA efficacy ranking is established. BUBR1 mediation is additionally needed only for a restoration claim, not to recognize a compensation endpoint.
competitiveness.next_evidence: An exposure-qualified controlled comparison of absolute useful output, renewable reserve and chromosome fidelity, accounting for all starting units and survival. Neither survivor percentage nor normalized force alone settles net benefit.

remaining_salt_followup.scope: The 2019 sodium-salt force study and 2021 dose/toxicity study are now separately qualified. The cholesterol paper retains only bounded lineage review pending full mechanistic appraisal; its force data are reused.
remaining_salt_followup.next_checks: Human association versus causal effect, distinct tracer cohort, isotope evidence versus pathway necessity, and exact cohort/endpoint lineage.

scope.clinical_regimen: None proposed; reported animal exposures are source descriptors.
scope.global_completeness: Broader enumeration and efficacy follow-up remain incomplete.

root_reading.main: Selected original preparation, experiment, results/captions, force methods and statistics passages; complete source qualification and lineage report. Not a second complete root main reading.
root_reading.native: All panels of native Figures 1, 2, 4 and 6; native supplement page 3. Figure images/axes and captions cross-checked; no numerical digitization or independent histopathological diagnosis.
root_reading.independent: Separate independent reviewer read complete main, all six native figures and ten supplement pages, plus bounded original lineage evidence; PASS without required correction.

additional_salt_source_qualification.scope: Injected D,L sodium-salt force evidence, including a reported 2019 absolute-force contrast, with survivor, allocation, toxicity and preparation limits. No oral-ester or MVA transfer.
